transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I suppose it’s a bit embarrassing. What finally made me come in is that sometimes after I’ve eaten too much, I go upstairs and make myself sick. Then I just pretend I’m tidying up or getting ready for bed.
Do you often feel like you're eating large amounts of food in a short period, and then feel out of control during these episodes?

Yes… I suppose so. If no one’s in the kitchen, I can sort of… keep going. Leftovers from a church supper, crackers and cheese, biscuits or cookies, whatever I’ve baked for book club. It can all happen in one sitting, much more than I’d ever put on a plate for a normal meal.
How often do you make yourself sick or do something else to try to control your weight or shape after these eating episodes?
Since last winter, I don’t think there’s really been a week without it… at least once. I’ll… make myself sick, or skip a meal after, or walk too much to try to undo it.
Can you tell me more about when you make yourself sick or use other ways to control your weight—does this happen after every large eating episode, or only sometimes?
Only sometimes… not every time. But when I feel I’ve eaten too much, I’ll often go upstairs and make myself throw up. Then I try to make it look like I’m just cleaning up or getting ready for bed.
How often do these large eating episodes happen—like, how many times a week or month would you say you eat this way?
Since last winter… it’s been most weeks, I think. Usually at least once a week that I have one of those… private eating spells. Not every day, but it hasn’t really stopped.
Do these episodes and the things you do afterward cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Yes… it does. I still manage at work, I get through the day at the optician’s, but I’m distracted by it more than I’d like to admit. And tired… worn down, really.

I’ve started avoiding some meals too, church things or family meals, because I worry about what I’ll do afterward with the food.
Do you feel unhappy with your body weight or shape, and does that influence how you eat or what you do after eating?

Yes… I suppose it does. My daughter, and someone at church, have said I look too thin, but I don’t really see it that way.

If my skirt feels tight, or the scale is even a pound up, I panic a bit. It feels like I’ve suddenly let myself get… huge, somehow. And then it affects what I eat, yes.

When you make yourself sick or do something else to control your weight, does it usually happen after you've eaten a very large amount, or does it sometimes happen even if you've only eaten a small or normal portion?

It’s mostly after I’ve eaten too much. That’s… what finally made me say something, really.

I’ll go upstairs afterward and make myself sick, then come back down and act like I was just tidying the kitchen or getting ready for bed.
Do you ever make yourself sick or do something else to control your weight even after eating a normal or small amount of food, or does it only happen after you've eaten a very large amount?

It’s… mainly when I’ve eaten too much. That’s the part that made me worry enough to say something.

I’ll go upstairs and make myself sick, and then just come back down as if I was tidying up or getting ready for bed.

Can you tell me more about the times you feel like you've eaten too much—do you feel like you're eating an unusually large amount of food in a short time, more than what most people would eat in the same situation?

Yes… I think so. I don’t like saying it, but it’s not just an extra helping.

If I’m alone in the kitchen, I might go through leftovers from a church supper, crackers and cheese, cookies… whatever I’ve baked for book club. All in one sitting. It’s much more than I’d ever put on a plate for a normal meal.
When you're eating during one of these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating, even if you wanted to?
Yes. Once I start, it’s like… something switches. I know I should stop, I’m even telling myself, “Linda, stop now,” but I just keep reaching for more.
Do you ever make yourself sick or do something else to control your weight even after eating a normal or small amount of food, or does it only happen after you've eaten a very large amount?

Mostly after I’ve eaten too much. That’s… what finally made me mention it.

I’ll go upstairs and make myself throw up, then come back down and act like I was just tidying up or getting ready for bed.

inference_history.note: The patient continues to endorse recurrent binge eating followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors (e.g., self-induced vomiting, excessive exercise), occurring at least once a week for several months. The behaviors cause significant distress and interfere with daily functioning. The patient is also unduly influenced by body shape and weight, with body image disturbance present. These features are consistent with both F50.2 (Bulimia nervosa) and F50.0 (Anorexia nervosa, binge-eating/purging type), which remain under consideration. No features rule out either diagnosis definitively at this time.

The patient confirms that purging behavior (self-induced vomiting) occurs mostly after large eating episodes, which supports F50.2 (Bulimia Nervosa). However, the presence of significant concern about body shape and weight, along with some avoidance of social eating situations and compensatory behaviors beyond purging (e.g., skipping meals, excessive walking), means F50.0 (Anorexia Nervosa) remains in the differential as weight and shape concerns are prominent and influence behavior. No new exclusion criteria for either diagnosis were identified this turn.
